newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Dresdner doubts SFR will soar after Euro.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner doubts SFR will soar after Euro.

text.p: Dresdner Bank AG chairman Juergen Sarrazin said he did not expect the Swiss franc to appreciate much further in connection with the introduction of Europe's single currency, the Euro.

Sarrazin told the German/Swiss Chamber of Commerce he expected the single currency to be introduced on time and to be a stable currency, and added that investors had to consider exchange rate risks and the low interest rates in Switzerland.
But if financial markets began to expect a delay in the switch to a single currency, capital transfers to Switzerland could increase, he said.

"This would in all likelihood lead to a further appreciation in the franc, harm Switzerland's exports, tourism and economic growth, and put the monetary policy of the central bank under pressure," Sarrazin said.

He also said an exchange rate risk always exists, even with a traditional safe haven currency such as the Swiss franc, mainly because the country cannot live with exchange rate extremes in light of its export and tourism industsries.
"In my opinion this view will also spread through financial markets," he said.

He added that the realistic alternatives facing Switzerland in connection with the third phase of Europe's economic and monetary union was to retain a floating exchange rate or to forge a link with the Euro.
A floating rate would enable Switzerland to retain its monetary autonomy, he said.
"By coupling the franc to the Euro this autonomy would hardly be limited because I expect an EMU made up of core countries committed to stability," he added.
At the same time Switzerland would be able to take advantage of firm or adjustable exchange rates, Sarrazin said.
"Switzerland and Germany are in this regard in the same boat. Both have a fundamental interest in the opportunities that a stable Euro offers," he said. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
